title: Heresy of the Naked Fold: The Prion Protein-Only Inheritance Hypothesis, Cofactor Catalysis, and the Prionoid Boundary on Trial — From Tikvah Alper's UV-resistant scrapie puzzle to Prusiner's 1982 protein-only manifesto; Büeler, Aguzzi & Weissmann's Prnp0/0 knockout immunity & gene-dosage lag; Wang & Ma's 2010 de novo E. coli recombinant prion fulfilling Koch's postulates; Halfmann & Lindquist's 700-strain wild yeast bet-hedging survey; Manuelidis's 25-nm slow-virus challenge, Supattapone's 10^6-fold phosphatidylethanolamine cofactor requirement & Soto's contagious prion vs. non-contagious Alzheimer/Parkinson prionoid taxonomy; Knowles-Vendruscolo fragmentation math & Eyring cofactor barriers

teenKit.tldr: Prions are rogue, shape-shifting proteins that can infect a brain and cause fatal disease without containing a single drop of DNA or RNA. They shatter the foundational rule of biology that says you need genes to replicate.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding prions forces medicine to rethink how neurodegenerative nightmares like Creutzfeldt-Jakob, Alzheimer's, and Parkinson's spread through the brain like cellular dominoes.
keyTakeaways: Biological physics dogma was shattered when scientists proved that biological infection and replication can happen through pure protein conformation change instead of genetic code.
Knockout experiments proved that a host organism needs its own normal copy of the prion protein to actually get sick, meaning the pathogen weaponizes the host's own biology.
While true prions like scrapie are actively contagious between individuals, related protein misfoldings in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's act locally inside a single brain as non-contagious 'prionoids'.

vocab.meaning: An infectious agent made entirely of misfolded protein that forces normal proteins to twist into the same deadly shape.
The classic biological rule stating that genetic information flows strictly from DNA to RNA to proteins.
A neurological symptom causing a total loss of full control over bodily movements and muscle coordination.
An extra molecule, like a specific lipid or RNA strand, that acts as a helper to catalyze the misfolding process.

quiz.question: What happens to a prion when it is blasted with UV light and enzymes designed to destroy DNA and RNA?
options: It completely disintegrates and loses all infectivity.
It mutates into a harmless ordinary protein.
It remains fully infectious because it contains zero nucleic acids.
It instantly turns into a standard virus.
quiz.explanation: Because prions lack DNA or RNA entirely, treatments that shred genetic material leave the rogue protein structure completely unaffected and dangerous.

quiz.question: Why did mice bred without any normal prion proteins (Prnp-knockout mice) survive being exposed to brain tissue full of scrapie?
options: Their immune systems aggressively manufactured antibodies against the prions.
They lacked the normal protein raw material for the prions to corrupt and stack.
The genetic knockout gave them complete immunity to all known viruses.
The scrapie extract decayed before it could reach their brains.
quiz.explanation: Prions propagate by forcing a host's normal proteins to misfold, so a mouse with zero normal prion proteins gives the infection nothing to latch onto or convert.

quiz.question: What is the key difference that separates true prions from Alzheimer's and Parkinson's 'prionoids'?
options: Prionoids are made of DNA, whereas true prions are made of fat.
True prions are naturally contagious between different organisms, while prionoids only self-seed within a single brain.
Prionoids only affect yeast cells, while true prions only affect hamsters.
There is zero biochemical difference between them.
quiz.explanation: While both involve self-propagating protein shapes, only true prions manage to cross organism boundaries and act as contagious infectious diseases.
